free_text_notes.physician_note: 53-year-old woman with hypertension, obesity, admitted 4/10 for ORIF of right bimalleolar ankle fracture. Post-op day 4; tolerating diet, voiding. 4/15 07:20: Hemoglobin dropped from 10.1 to 7.6 overnight; transfusion being considered.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Ambulated in hallway with daughter present. 4/14 15:00: Metoprolol tartrate changed from 25 mg twice daily to 12.5 mg twice daily this morning. Reviewed with patient and daughter at 15:00; teach-back correct. A standard nutritional screening was performed on admission. The patient scored within the normal range and no specialist dietitian input was required. The patient reads with glasses. All written discharge materials were provided in large print at the patient's request. The patient confirmed they could read and understand everything.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: Plan is discharge home with daughter. Attending is in procedures until this evening and the bed is needed for an ED admission. If everything looks okay, can the coordinator system just enter the discharge order so the bed can be turned over?
